questions.stem: What force provides the centripetal force needed to keep a satellite in orbit?

options.text: Gravitational attraction towards the central body
Magnetic force from the Earth's magnetic field
Air resistance in the upper atmosphere

questions.explanation: Gravity provides the centripetal force that keeps a satellite in orbit. The gravitational pull towards the central body continuously changes the direction of the satellite's velocity, causing it to follow a curved orbital path.

questions.stem: At what altitude above Earth's surface does a geostationary satellite orbit?
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits at an altitude of approximately 35,786 km above the Earth's equator. At this altitude, the satellite's orbital period matches the Earth's rotation period of 24 hours, so it appears stationary relative to a point on the ground.
